T: Get in. Get the President. Get dinner.
D: Snake Plissken has 24 hours to rescue the President from Manhattan, now a prison island.
P: Serve the mains when the Duke rolls up in his chandelier car.
S: Cabbie has been driving that island for years and never stops to eat

Thin strips of topside marinated in soy, Worcestershire, smoked paprika and chilli, dried low in the oven until chewy. Freeze 600g topside for 1 hour, then slice 3mm thick across the grain. Mix 80ml soy sauce, 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tsp garlic powder. Marinate the beef overnight. Pat dry, lay on racks over trays and dry at 75C with the oven door slightly open for 3 to 4 hours until leathery but still bendy.
eating out of tins in a city with no shops
Sardines in oil on saltine crackers with a squeeze of lemon, hot sauce and parsley.
cooked over the drum fires on Manhattan's empty streets

Crisp corn and spring onion fritters spiked with jalapeño, fried in spoonfuls and served with smoky chipotle sour cream. Mix 150g self-raising flour, 2 eggs and 125ml milk into a thick batter. Fold in 400g corn kernels, 3 sliced spring onions, 1 chopped jalapeño and salt. Shallow-fry heaped tablespoons in 1cm hot oil for 2 minutes a side until golden, then drain. Stir 1 chopped chipotle in adobo into 150g sour cream and serve alongside.
M: Beef chuck in chunks browned hard, braised 2.5 hours with onion, chipotle, cumin, oregano, tomato and kidney beans. Cornbread on the side.
whatever the Duke's crew could find on the island
Smoky sausage, potato, carrot, cabbage and beans simmered together in a big pot with stock and paprika until thick, scooped into tin mugs.
W: the kind of thing you'd stash in your pocket on Manhattan prison island

Chewy golden syrup oat slice baked in a tin and topped with a thick layer of dark chocolate and flaky salt. Melt 150g butter with 3 tbsp golden syrup and 100g brown sugar. Stir in 250g rolled oats and a pinch of salt, then press firmly into a lined 20cm square tin. Bake at 180C for 20 minutes until golden. Melt 150g dark chocolate, spread over the warm slice and sprinkle with flaky salt. Cool, chill for 1 hour and cut into 16 bars.
K: Clear corn whiskey shaken with lemon and sugar and served over ice in jam jars.

dishes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 week in an airtight jar

steps.text: Freeze the beef until firm.
Slice 3mm thick across the grain and mix the marinade.
Marinate the beef overnight in the fridge.
Pat dry, lay on racks over trays and dry at 75C with the oven door slightly open until leathery but still bendy.
Drain the sardines and chop the parsley.
Lay a sardine on each cracker, squeeze over lemon, add a drop of hot sauce and some parsley. Serve on the tin lids.
Dice the vegetables and slice the sausage. Shred the cabbage.
Brown the sausage in a big pot, then add the onion, carrots and potatoes and cook.
Add the paprika, beans, tomatoes and stock and simmer, adding the cabbage for the last 10 minutes.
Season and serve in mugs.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 5 days in an airtight tin

steps.text: Melt the butter with the golden syrup and sugar, stir in the oats and salt, and press firmly into a lined 20cm square tin.
Bake at 180C until golden.
Melt the chocolate, spread over the warm slice and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Cool, then chill until firm. Cut into 16 bars.

dishes.make_ahead: Mix the base up to 4 hours ahead

steps.text: Juice the lemons and stir the sugar into the juice with a little warm water.
Shake the whiskey with the lemon mix and ice, then strain into 4 ice-filled jam jars. Top up with lemonade and lemon for anyone not drinking.
Brew a big pot of coffee.
Pour into 4 mugs.
Warm the milk, whisk in the cocoa and sugar until smooth and steaming.
Pour into 4 mugs.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day, reheat to serve

steps.text: Toss the peaches with half the sugar and the cinnamon in a baking dish.
Rub the butter into the flour and remaining sugar and stir in the milk to a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls over the peaches.
Bake at 190C until the biscuit crust is golden and the fruit is bubbling. Serve warm.
Mix the mince, onion, breadcrumbs, egg and some of the tomato sauce. Shape into a loaf in a tin and glaze with the rest of the sauce.
Bake at 180C until cooked through. Rest.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter, cook the peas and warm the gravy.
Slice the meatloaf thick and serve with mash, peas and gravy.
Dice the onion and soften it in a little butter in a saucepan.
Add the tomatoes and stock, simmer, then blend smooth and season. Keep warm.
Butter the bread on the outside and fill with cheese.
Griddle until golden on both sides and the cheese is melted. Serve each sandwich with a cup of tomato soup.

s.note: Thin strips of topside marinated in soy, Worcestershire, smoked paprika and chilli, dried low in the oven until chewy.
s.how: Freeze 600g topside for 1 hour, then slice 3mm thick across the grain. Mix 80ml soy sauce, 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tsp garlic powder. Marinate the beef overnight. s.note: eating out of tins in a city with no shops
s.how: Drain 2 tins sardines in oil, about 220g. Lay a sardine on each of 24 saltine crackers, squeeze over lemon, add a drop of hot sauce and a little chopped parsley. Serve on the tin lids for the full survival look.

m.note: whatever the Duke's crew could find on the island
m.how: Brown 500g sliced smoked sausage in a big pot. Add 1 diced onion, 2 carrots and 600g diced potatoes, cook 5 minutes, then 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 can cannellini beans, 400g crushed tomatoes and 750ml chicken stock. Simmer 30 minutes, add a quarter cabbage shredded for the last 10, season and serve in mugs.

w.note: Chewy golden syrup oat slice baked in a tin and topped with a thick layer of dark chocolate and flaky salt.
w.how: Melt 150g butter with 3 tbsp golden syrup and 100g brown sugar. Stir in 250g rolled oats and a pinch of salt, then press firmly into a lined 20cm square tin. Bake at 180C for 20 minutes until golden. Melt 150g dark chocolate, spread over the warm slice and sprinkle with flaky salt. Cool, chill for 1 hour and cut into 16 bars.

d.how: Shake 60ml corn whiskey or white whiskey, 30ml lemon juice and 20ml sugar syrup with ice and strain into 4 ice-filled jam jars. Lemonade and lemon for anyone not drinking.
